" alt= " Guitarist Vic Juris at the NAC 's Fourth Stage in Ottawa , Ont. , Feb. 28 , 2009. " data-portal-copyright= " Christopher Pike " **28;7395;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1531890 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vic Juris , a jazz guitarist of astounding abilities perhaps best known for his 23-year tenure in David Liebman&amp;rsquo ; s band , died Tuesday morning , according to a message on his Facebook page attributed to his friend and fellow guitarist Dave Stryker. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The New Jersey-based Juris , was 66 . He was diagnosed six months ago , after unexplainable fatigue on his gigs , with metastatic liver cancer . A GoFundMe campaign launched soon after raised more than $110,000 from fans and friends to help cover his treatment and living expenses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Juris played in Ottawa in 2008 with Liebman&amp;rsquo ; s group at the now-shuttered Cafe Paradiso on Bank Street , and that appearance led to further gigs and concerts here with Ottawa musicians John Geggie and Roddy Ellias. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2009 , before his National Arts Centre Fourth Stage concert Juris , Geggie said : &amp;ldquo ; Lots of people are aware of guitarists like John Scofield , John Abercrombie , Pat Metheny , Bill Frisell and Kurt Rosenwinkel , &amp;rdquo ; Geggie says . &amp;ldquo ; I feel Vic should be added to that exclusive list . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Geggie said that Juris&amp;rsquo ; s playing at Paradiso with Liebman had completely knocked him out . &amp;ldquo ; The fluid lyricism , the subtle phrasing , the engaging harmonies , the way he used his pedals as well as the classical guitar . They were revelations for me. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Juris , who was as humble and down-to-earth as he was talented , simply told this newspaper in 2009 : &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve played with just about everybody I wanted to play with , which is really a good thing . And , you know , there&amp;rsquo ; s not room for everybody at the forefront . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Juris&amp;rsquo ; s peers had the highest respect for him . The late John Abercrombie called him &amp;ldquo ; the greatest &amp;hellip ; there is none better anywhere . &amp;rdquo ; Metheny credited Juris for &amp;ldquo ; inventing new ways of thinking about jazz , harmonically and melodically. &amp;rdquo ; Frisell called him &amp;ldquo ; a total monster . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Juris&amp;rsquo ; s Facebook page , Stryker wrote : &amp;ldquo ; I am sorry to report that Vic Juris passed away this morning . Vic will live on through his music , as a beautiful person and through his many students . &amp;rdquo ; Here are Stryker , on the left , and Juris , on the right , playing a duet a few years ago : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;7425;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;7461;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Geggie says he decided to invite Juris to be part of his series after hearing the guitarist perform last April as part of saxophonist Dave Liebman&amp;rsquo ; s dynamic quartet at Caf&amp;eacute ; Paradiso. &amp;ldquo ; The whole band was stunning &amp;hellip ; a life-changing event for a lot of people , &amp;rdquo ; the bassist says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When my former colleague Doug Fischer interviewed Juris in 2009 , he put it to the guitarist that his stylistic versatility and range kept him from acquiring the profile of his more famous contemporaries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Juris replied : &amp;ldquo ; There might be something to that theory . have always been interested in all kinds of music and styles . I like crossing boundaries . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I had just a few very pleasant conversations with Juris , and this on-the-record exchange in early 2009 : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Q : What 's the difference between good music and bad music ? &lt;/b&gt; &lt;br&gt; A : What I decide I like and what I decide I don&amp;rsquo ; t like . I am at a point in my life where either I like something or I don&amp;rsquo ; t like it . And that can happen for a variety of reasons , but there is a connection or there is not . Whether it&amp;rsquo ; s good or bad is really up to the individual . The listener determines that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Q : If you could have dinner with any jazz figure , dead or alive , who would it be , and why ? &lt;/b&gt; &lt;br&gt; A : Wes Montgomery . He&amp;rsquo ; s always been my favourite guitarist . I think he&amp;rsquo ; d be an interesting guy to hang out with , to spend some time with , talking and maybe jamming a bit . Probably he&amp;rsquo ; d give me a lesson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Q : What 's the main thing you 're working on these days ? &lt;/b&gt; &lt;br&gt; A : I am working with a teacher in Boston named &lt;a href= " http : **34;7497;TOOLONG ... title= " Charliebanacos.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Charlie Banacos&lt;/a&gt; . We&amp;rsquo ; re working on all kinds of different harmonic and rhythmic challenges . It&amp;rsquo ; s been going on for years . He&amp;rsquo ; s a well-known teacher up there . We do it by correspondence . He sends me the music . We send cassette tapes back and forth . I guess it&amp;rsquo ; s old fashioned but cassettes are such an easy format . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Q : What are your three desert island recordings ? &lt;/b&gt; &lt;br&gt; 1 ) The Beatles , &lt;i&gt;Rubber Soul&lt;/i&gt; . Decade after decade I keep going back to it . The songs on that record are just incredible . It was kind of a departure for the Beatles . They played a more acoustic thing and it&amp;rsquo ; s just all so fantastic . &lt;br&gt; 2 ) Jimmy Smith and Wes Montgomery , &lt;i&gt;Dynamic Duo&lt;/i&gt; . It&amp;rsquo ; s just a classic . Pure joy . &lt;br&gt; 3 ) John&amp;rsquo ; s Coltrane&amp;rsquo ; s **26;7533;TOOLONG . It&amp;rsquo ; s the Bible for ballad playing . I go there for inspiration all the time . It never sounds old . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Q : If you were n't a musician , what do you think you 'd be doing ? &lt;/b&gt; &lt;br&gt; A : Oh , probably photography . I don&amp;rsquo ; t do it as much as I like to , but it&amp;rsquo ; s always been something I want to pursue , to get better at . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born Victor Jurusz in Jersey City , New Jersey , Juris took up the guitar in the early 1960s after listening to his father&amp;rsquo ; s Chuck Berry and Howlin&amp;rsquo ; Wolf records . Soon he was swept up in the rock explosion , especially the British invasion , and like many teenagers of the era he played in rock bands . He listed Beatles&amp;rsquo ; songs among his favourites . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the early &amp;rsquo ; 70s , he landed a jazz gig with bop-rooted organist Don Patterson , an encounter that led to work with Jimmy Smith , Wild Bill Davis and eventually regular stints in the bands of Phil Woods , Dizzy Gillespie and Chico Hamilton . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By the mid-&amp;rsquo ; 70s , he was juggling jazz with fusion , performing with Barry Miles and Eric Kloss , and first encountering Liebman , who was also heavy into fusion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the mid-&amp;rsquo ; 80s , Juris had a year-long stint in a guitar duo with Larry Coryell , and later teamed up with the young gypsy guitar improviser Bir&amp;eacute ; li Lagr&amp;egrave ; ne for a European tour and a recording . Among many other projects , he was a member of the Gary Peacock Quartet and musical director of a guitar quintet devoted to the music of Charles Mingus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He joined Liebman&amp;rsquo ; s band in 1991 , and taught at Rutgers and Lehigh universities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Facebook , Liebman wrote Wednesday morning : &amp;ldquo ; There was no one more real then Vic both as a person and musician . His sense of humour , honesty , sweet nature and musical skills were legendary . Vic was a &amp;lsquo ; nice guy&amp;rsquo ; in the true sense of the cliche , always ready to give a helping hand . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was best man at Kate and Vic&amp;rsquo ; s wedding while he spent twenty-three years with me going around the world to present our music . He was the hardest worker I have known , bringing a tape recorder to rehearsals , imploring me to play a voicing a few more times on the piano to be sure he understood it . Then taking it home to practice . Dedication beyond the norm . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;7561;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;7597;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;7633;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;7668;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;7704;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;7740;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Juris continued to gig despite his cancer , and he performed a few days before Christmas at Zinc Bar in New York with his trio . On Christmas Day , he posted a photo of himself with the gift that his wife , vocalist Kate Baker , gave to him &amp;mdash ; a beautiful guitar , of course &amp;mdash ; and wrote : &amp;rdquo ; I have been blessed by overwhelming support by you as I continue to fight the evil giant . He ain&amp;rsquo ; t gon na get me ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two recordings that Juris recently made have yet to be released , said publicist Lydia Liebman , who is Dave Liebman&amp;rsquo ; s daughter . That goes not only for saxophonist and bracing composer Quinsin Nachoff , whose mind-expanding double album tops my list , thanks to its broad range of stimulations and the intense and creative contributions of saxophonist David Binney and Nachoff himself , keyboard wizard Matt Mitchell and drummers Kenny Wollesen and Nate Wood . Also thrumming with rigorous , innovative sounds from expanded ensembles were the highly stimulating albums by reeds player Anna Webber and pianist Kris Davis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;8338;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8373;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8409;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8445;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Moving in another direction , North Carolina bassist and educator Steve Haines , an Ottawa native , released a beautiful orchestral album . Haines&amp;rsquo ; project featured the impeccable vocalist Becca Stevens singing a program that leaned heavily into Canadiana ( think Gordon Lightfoot , Kim Mitchell , Leonard Cohen ) , her voice wafting over lush accompaniment and offset by soloists Chad Eby and Joey Calderazzo. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;8481;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8516;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8552;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8588;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Montreal saxophonist Joel Miller went out on a limb with his own orchestral project that held multiple genres in its embrace&amp;hellip ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;8624;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8659;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;hellip ; while he played a starring role on the album of his friend , Montreal bassist Fraser Hollins , whose quartet was completed by no less than pianist Jon Cowherd and drummer Brian Blade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;8695;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps I&amp;rsquo ; m betraying a bias here , but tenor saxophonists took the lion&amp;rsquo ; s share of honours in my list , from Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s Mike Murley , definitively interpreting Kenny Wheeler&amp;rsquo ; s music in the multi-national band The North , which also features David Braid&amp;rsquo ; s incisive piano playing , to Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Mike Allen , who paid a visit to New York and made a casual and effortlessly swinging masterpiece with bassist Peter Washington and drummer Lewis Nash . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;8737;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8773;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;8809;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Toronto tenor tandem of Pat LaBarbera and Kirk MacDonald made clear why they&amp;rsquo ; re such musical treasures with a live album in which they roared through John Coltrane&amp;rsquo ; s music , from the conventionally bopping to the harmonically ornate to the momentously modal . Meanwhile , Montreal hornman Yannick Rieu&amp;rsquo ; s MachiNations was as eclectic and electric can be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;8851;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8893;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8929;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; With a French rhythm section , Vancouver-raised saxophonist Seamus Blake presented more of his fine , ear-catching compositions , which can be overshadowed because he is such a ferocious and engrossing soloist . Blake&amp;rsquo ; s one-time roommate in New York , Vancouver-based pianist John Stetch , continued to plumb his own heady and captivating depths with his own new band . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8965;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;9001;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;9037;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;9079;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; For pure saxophony , no record could top the elaborate pleasures of the Four Visions Saxophone Quartet , a project masterminded by Montreal saxophonist Samuel Blais that enlisted the formidable Americans David Binney , Dave Liebman and Donny McCaslin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;9121;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; More off-the-cuff were the nonetheless pristine duo albums from alto saxophonist veteran PJ Perry and pianist Bill Mays , and , from the vaults , an early 1990s gigging document from bassist Don Thompson and the late American guitar star John Abercrombie. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;9163;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Saxophonist Murley also made the above list a second time for his chamber-y collaboration with stalwart collaborators Reg Schwager on guitar and bassist Steve Wallace , with pianist Renee Rosnes guesting and adding her special panache . It was also nice to hear Rosnes apply her talents to the album&amp;rsquo ; s two Kenny Wheeler tunes , as every Canadian jazz-person should . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Speaking of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s vital jazz pianists , the country can now claim German-born pianist Florian Hoefner , who resides in Newfoundland , as one of its own . Hoefner , who became a Canadian citizen , released a wonderful trio record this year with the Toronto rhythm team of bassist Andrew Downing and drummer Nick Fraser helping him to bring his music to life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;9205;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;9241;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Toronto guitarist Ted Quinlan marked his recent retirement from Humber College with a quartet album showing off his warm sound and sophisticated lyricism , bolstered by his long-time friends and elite musicians Brian Dickinson at the piano , bassist Kieran Overs and drummer Ted Warren . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;9277;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;9312;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The young Montreal drummer Louis-Vincent Hamel released a dark-hued album that was the year&amp;rsquo ; s best debut by a Canadian jazz player , powered by performances by saxophonist Alex Francoeur , trumpeter Simon Millerd , pianist Rafael Zaldivar , bassist Mike De Masi and the drummer&amp;rsquo ; s father , guitarist Gabriel Hamel. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 120 " style= " position : relative ; display : block ; width : 100% ; height : 120px ; " src= " **40;9348;TOOLONG ... allowtransparency= " true " frameborder= " 0 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; The best release from a Canadian jazz vocalist came from the other side of the country , in the form of Karin Plato&amp;rsquo ; s This Could Be The One , on which pianist Chris Gestrin and clarinetist James Danderfer distinguished themselves . &lt;/p&gt; ArtsFor her fifth album , jazz singer-songwriter Diane Nalini focuses on the futurehttp : **34;10417;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;10453;TOOLONG ... title= " Diane Nalini. " alt= " Diane Nalini. " data-portal-copyright= " Adrian Cho " **28;10489;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1525404 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Singer-songwriter Diane Nalini allowed a decade to pass between the release of her fourth and fifth albums &amp;mdash ; with good reason . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First , there was the matter of her impressive career in the federal public service . In the last 10 years , Nalini , a Rhodes Scholar with a doctorate in applied nuclear physics , worked first on climate change policy at Environment Canada before moving most recently to Natural Resources Canada to turn her attention to nuclear energy policy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not as if Nalini had just set music-making aside . She&amp;rsquo ; s been plenty active as the resident vocalist of the Ottawa Jazz Orchestra , and performed some of her songs in that setting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , Nalini says : &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t think I expected to go so long between albums . I&amp;rsquo ; ve been doing a lot musically over the past few years , but never found the right time to make a new album until I finally took three months off to work on it full-time . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The result of Nalini&amp;rsquo ; s fall 2018 sabbatical is her album Future Perfect , a collection of 13 songs she and her band will launch Saturday during two concerts at the National Arts Centre&amp;rsquo ; s Fourth Stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During the first month of her time away , Nalini took songs she had written in recent years and crafted arrangements for the band that would record them , paying particular attention to determining precise tempo markings for her material . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Especially for passages where the lyrics are dense , it can really kill a tune if you count it in too fast . It won&amp;rsquo ; t breathe right , &amp;rdquo ; Nalini says . &amp;ldquo ; Conversely , if you count a tune in too slowly , it can become a dirge . So I do that work ahead of time so that there won&amp;rsquo ; t be false starts in the studio because of a count-in that was too fast or slow . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A month into her hiatus , Nalini recorded in Montreal , where she grew up and lived before studying at Oxford University . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Joining her in the studio over three days were her long-time friends and collaborators Dany Roy on tenor saxophone , guitarist Mike Rud , bassist Alec Walkington and drummer Camil B&amp;eacute ; lisle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They made everything sound even better than it could in my head ! &amp;rdquo ; says Nalini. &amp;ldquo ; Every one of them is so talented and yet very humble and grounded . And so musical . I love the way they listen , and when we all listen to each other and have musical conversations with space to breathe , that&amp;rsquo ; s when the magic happens . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All but Rud , who this year moved to B.C. , will be at the Fourth Stage . Ottawa guitarist Tim Bedner will step in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After the session , Nalini spent time reviewing rough mixes and choosing the best takes . Her mixing sessions were mostly finished last December . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her new album is called Future Perfect , although there is no song on the recording with that title . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As I put together the list of songs that I wanted to record , I realized that every one of them dealt with the future in some way , &amp;rdquo ; Nalini says . &amp;ldquo ; Either they explored my hopes and dreams for the future , or concerns about the future of the planet , or a sense of nostalgia for a love that might have been in an alternate future . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The new album reflects Nalini&amp;rsquo ; s growth as a vocalist and songwriter. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As a vocalist , I&amp;rsquo ; ve become more disciplined about regular practice , including working more on technique and physical endurance . This is crucial when singing with a big band , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve also been doing more teaching , helping singers who want to develop good jazz phrasing and who want to start improvising . This definitely builds more awareness of one&amp;rsquo ; s own process for unpacking harmony . As a result , I&amp;rsquo ; m much more aware of my own instrument . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The album also includes Nalini&amp;rsquo ; s able scat-singing , which did not figure on her previous recordings . &amp;ldquo ; On my new album , I improvised on several tracks and I had lots of fun engaging in musical conversations with the musicians , throwing melodic themes back and forth at each other , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a songwriter , Nalini recently found a new tool to help her &amp;mdash ; the ukulele. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve fallen in love with the tenor and baritone ukulele , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; After some misadventures with acoustic guitar some years ago , I was left feeling it was just too big for my hands . I still used it for composing , but it never seemed to fit . Enter the ukulele . I can noodle on it while sitting on the sofa and it&amp;rsquo ; s small enough to travel with . I took it with me to an artist residency in Spain in 2017 to complete some of the songs for this album . It&amp;rsquo ; s a brilliant songwriting tool . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In true polymath fashion , Nalini writes and sings music in four languages &amp;mdash ; English , French , Spanish and Portuguese . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love singing in different languages because they really bring out a completely different aspect of my personality , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Each language has unique expressions that don&amp;rsquo ; t have their exact equivalent in the other . The metaphors and jokes are completely different . It&amp;rsquo ; s a different way of thinking . And therefore also a different way of singing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If I had to over-simplify , I&amp;rsquo ; d say Brazilian Portuguese has a soft , sensual and syncopated quality that is the perfect vehicle for bossa nova . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;10519;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;10555;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Spanish is passionate and dramatic . French is romantic and sarcastic . English is the language of Shakespeare and of jazz and blues . So taken together , that&amp;rsquo ; s an emotional journey worth taking . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nalini says that while Future Perfect is &amp;ldquo ; definitely a jazz album , &amp;rdquo ; it covers a lot of ground with the subjects of its songs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are love songs , songs about wonder , about the joys of little things , songs about needing solace , facing an uncertain future but staying strong . ArtsMeet Peter Woods , the Ottawa minister who marries jazz and spiritualityhttp : **28;11580;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;11610;TOOLONG ... title= " Minister Peter Woods , who is also a saxophonist , and is combining music , spirituality and community building at several events next weekend . " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;11646;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1504219 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you ask Peter Woods to name some of his heroes , the minister of MacKay United Church in New Edinburgh offers an eclectic response . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For example , Woods looks up to Pastor Miguel Tomas Castro Garcia , a Salvadoran activist and baptist preacher who mentored him in the 1980s when Woods was living in Central America and doing human rights work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Woods , who is 56 and was ordained almost three decades ago , also counts as a major influence the Canadian poet and philosopher Jan Zwicky , whose work helps him ponder the connection between faith and art . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And because Woods is a busy saxophonist around Ottawa , he reveres some of jazz history&amp;rsquo ; s most swinging and big-toned horn players . He confesses to a particular obsession with the late , gruff-toned saxman Gene Ammons &amp;ldquo ; as a player and as a spiritual force . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indeed , Woods says that for him , music and spirituality are deeply intertwined . Throughout his life as a minister , &amp;ldquo ; music has been the governing image of the divine &amp;hellip ; and gigging has truly been a sort of spiritual practice , &amp;rdquo ; Woods says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Later this week , Woods will play a run of especially spiritual gigs involving some of his Ottawa-based collaborators plus a special guest from Toronto , Tom Reynolds , who is both a jazz pianist and a professor of theology at the University of Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s Emmanuel College . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Woods grew up in Ottawa and began his musical exploits as a trombonist at Broadview Public School and Nepean High School . He switched to saxophone after high school and took some private lessons . He also took degrees in literature and theology , eventually leading to a master of divinity degree . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the last decade and a half , Woods played extensively and recorded with the late Ottawa jazz pianist Brian Browne , enjoying &amp;ldquo ; a wonderful and ambitious gig-based educational odyssey , &amp;rdquo ; Woods says . He and Browne were involved in a duo project that Woods called Jazz in Sacred Spaces , which allowed them to play concerts from Alberta to Nova Scotia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;11676;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;11711;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Woods says theology and music have been involved in a &amp;ldquo ; beautifully endless conversation&amp;rdquo ; for centuries , from the songs of King David to medieval chants to Bach to gospel music to Duke Ellington . Ammons , the earthy , bluesy saxophonist , recorded an album called Preachin&amp;rsquo ; , which Woods says &amp;ldquo ; speaks straight to me for its frank simplicity as an inspired testimony . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Woods also finds a seam of contemplative spirituality in the much more European and meditative music exemplified by the ECM Records label catalogue . The minister and pianist Mitchell Wright , MacKay&amp;rsquo ; s musical director , will improvise music for meditation every Tuesday this month at 7 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The spiritual force of music &amp;ldquo ; has the potential to be evoked at almost any gig being played in Ottawa tonight , &amp;rdquo ; adds Woods . &amp;ldquo ; I think my appetite for life as a working musician is borne out of a curiosity to see whether that surprising and magical quality will emerge on the gig tonight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; From Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s Roddy Ellias to Tim Bedner and Miguel De Armas , there are so many great players at all levels of jazz who work a deeply creative vein of spirituality , &amp;rdquo ; Woods says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the summer of 2015 , Woods began at MacKay , where the leadership team , he says , &amp;ldquo ; encouraged a deep pursuit of artistic expression , theological reflection and community engagement . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest expression of Woods&amp;rsquo ; jazz-based work at MacKay is what he calls the Kindness of Jazz project . Woods says he&amp;rsquo ; s addressing such questions as &amp;ldquo ; How do faith communities engage in social and spiritual improvisation ? &amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; How do I best integrate the depth of wisdom and reflection that jazz musicians bring to bear on these contemporary and ancient themes ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s partly about finding opportunities to improvise music in sacred and communal settings , and partly about how that improvisation reflects on communal values , &amp;rdquo ; Woods says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of Woods&amp;rsquo ; gigs this weekend with jazz pianist Reynolds will be a quartet performance at the first Beechwood Night Market , which will be hosted by MacKay on Friday from 6 to 10 p.m . She sang in a choir for 10 years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But it was only at 15 that she came to the instrument at the centre of the music she makes today &amp;mdash ; the drums . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I taught myself when I was 15 and started to take lessons when I was 16 , &amp;rdquo ; recalls the German musician who is in her early 30s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was fascinated by the independence of a drummer and by the power of the instrument , &amp;rdquo ; she continues . &amp;ldquo ; Especially in jazz music , I always loved the freedom , and that one song can sound completely different each time you play it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These days , Wiening pursues jazz on two continents , splitting her time between New York City and Cologne . She and her New York-based quintet play GigSpace in Ottawa on Sunday night as part of a short Ontario tour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The concert in the cosy 46-seat space on Gladstone Avenue will consist of Wiening&amp;rsquo ; s elaborate but lyrical compositions , which are documented on her just-released album Metropolis Paradise on the esteemed Greenleaf Music label . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;12309;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;12345;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Wiening is steeped in musical education . I feel like I grew artistically and that would not have been possible in Germany , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of her most influential teachers was vibraphonist Stefon Harris , with whom she studied composition and harmony . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; His approach to improvising , composing , harmony , ear training and communicating within the band had a huge impact on my playing and my relationship to music , &amp;rdquo ; Wiening says . &amp;ldquo ; It opened up a whole other world to me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; With the drums , I was always missing the melodic part that I&amp;rsquo ; m used to from the piano . I don&amp;rsquo ; t want to give that up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Of course , the music scene and the artistic value of New York is not comparable to any other place in the world . I&amp;rsquo ; d like to have both , if possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When asked if it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to make a living as a jazz musician in an age of streaming and declining album sales , Wiening responds that the jazz life has always been challenging . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Jazz musicians don&amp;rsquo ; t do it for money , &amp;rdquo ; she adds . &amp;ldquo ; If I&amp;rsquo ; d like to be famous and rich , I can go ahead and play pop music . But I don&amp;rsquo ; t want to do that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Jazz is a decision , and if you really work hard , it&amp;rsquo ; s possible to make a living , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Mareike Wiening Quintet&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Sunday , Nov. 3 at 7:30 p.m. &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; GigSpace ( 953 Gladstone Ave. ) &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets : &lt;/strong&gt; $25 at &lt;a href= " http : //gigspace.ca " &gt;gigspace.ca&lt;/ ... , or by calling 613-729-0693 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Mareike Wiening Quintet also plays : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; Thursday , Oct. 31 at the Rex Jazz and Blues Bar in Toronto &lt;br&gt; Friday , Nov. 1 at PUASA art house in Buffalo , NY &lt;br&gt; Saturday , Nov. 2 at the Jazz Room in Kitchener &lt;br&gt; Tuesday , Nov. 5 at the Jazz Gallery in New York &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;12524;TOOLONG " **32;12551;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **28;12585;TOOLONG " &gt;o ... &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumWed , 30 Oct 2019 19:18:22 **45;12615;TOOLONG ... ArtsFlorian Hoefner Trio CD reviewedhttp : **32;12662;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;12696;TOOLONG ... title= " Florian Hoefner Trio , with drummer Nick Fraser and bassist Andrew Downing . " data-portal-copyright= " BO HUANG " **28;12732;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1473003 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;First Spring ( Alma Records ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Florian Hoefner Trio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If I recall correctly , Florian Hoefner , the exceptional German-born jazz pianist now based in St. John&amp;rsquo ; s , Nfld. , became a Canadian citizen this year . Given that his new album , First Spring , includes an original track entitled Winter in June , I&amp;rsquo ; d say Hoefner gets Canada as well as anyone born here . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You might even call his new album , First Spring , his most Canadian album yet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yes , the influence of living on the Rock for the last few years &amp;mdash ; Hoefner teaches at Memorial University , as does his Canadian-born wife , clarinetist Christine Carter &amp;mdash ; can clearly be discerned on selected tracks on his most recent albums , the solo album Coldwater Stories and the quartet album Luminosity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But First Spring , which was released in late September and which is being feted during the next few nights at trio gigs in Toronto , Hamilton and Montreal , marks Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s first work with an all-Canadian group . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On his first trio album , he&amp;rsquo ; s joined by the wonderfully in-sync bass-and-drums pair from Toronto , bassist Andrew Downing and drummer Nick Fraser . The trio breathes life beautifully into nine tracks that in the main brings Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s jazz-based musical sensibility to bear on a diverse collection of folk-music material . This strategy strikes me as a bit of a Canadian jazz predilection , if not exclusively so . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Opening the album is Hound&amp;rsquo ; s Tune . With it , Hoefner puts his trio&amp;rsquo ; s bold stamp on a piece by the late Newfoundland fiddle master Rufus Guinchard . A crucial component on this effervescent opener is Downing&amp;rsquo ; s dazzling arco playing , which reappears elsewhere on First Spring with the impact of a separate instrument . Here&amp;rsquo ; s exactly how that tune went down : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;12762;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;12798;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The album takes a sombre , bluesy turn with the trio&amp;rsquo ; s run through Calvary , Levon Helm&amp;rsquo ; s rumbling , twanging epic . This patient track transforms Helm&amp;rsquo ; s gravelly version without losing its essence , and is spacious but also rich with the kinds of arranged intricacies that grace Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s work with the German co-op quintet Subtone. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hoefner returns to the Americana well for a rendition of Sam Amidon&amp;rsquo ; s simple lament Short Life . On this track , Downing offers another soulful star turn with his bowing and Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s playing is at its most bell-like before he ratchets up the tension during his improvisation , well shadowed by Fraser . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Hoefner roams further afield when the trio addresses the sad strains of the Armenian folk song Loosin Yelav . With its glowing expressiveness and mature way , the trio brings to mind a Keith Jarrett Trio performance . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then , the trio launches into its take on the waltzing Scottish folk song The Maid on the Shore , a minor-key romp that eventually charges ahead with an unabashedly swinging vibe. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Three Hoefner originals are woven into the flow of the album , and they mesh well with the other material and broaden the thrust of the disc . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The captivating title track , written for Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s young son Max , and Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s piece Solstice are lighter and more buoyant than the album&amp;rsquo ; s more plaintive tracks . Solstice in particular is a surging , charging tune . Both tracks benefit from Fraser&amp;rsquo ; s impeccable musicality , which allows him to propel music and make it vividly colourful at the same time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s piece Winter in June is slower and more meditative before it thaws out and becomes more spirited . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;12834;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;12870;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Closing the album is an austere rendition of the traditional piece Rain and Snow &amp;mdash ; a companion piece to Winter in June ? &amp;mdash ; that brings an exquisite and beautifully recorded album to a fine point of rest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Having heard Hoefner now on record and in person performing solo and with a quartet , a quintet and now a trio , I&amp;rsquo ; m stumped as to which context I prefer him in . In every situation , the music is so substantial and at times even breath-taking . I do know that I&amp;rsquo ; ll be coming back to First Spring for more enjoyable listens , to appreciate its forthright beauty and this new expansiveness of Hoefner&amp;rsquo ; s musical world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;The Florian Hoefner Trio plays : &lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Thursday , Oct. 24 at 9:30 p.m. at the Rex Jazz and Blues Bar in Toronto ( with Andrew Downing and Jim Doxas ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Friday , Oct. 25 at 7 p.m. at the Conservatory in Hamilton ( with Andrew Downing and Nick Fraser ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Saturday , Oct. 26 at 6:30 p.m. at Diese Onze in Montreal ( with Adrian Vedady and Jim Doxas ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;12906;TOOLONG " **32;12933;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **28;12967;TOOLONG " &gt;o ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumThu , 24 Oct 2019 19:32:52 **45;12997;TOOLONG ... think of J.J. I also became more open to and interested in free jazz . I hope to add in some way to his legacy of bringing art of the highest integrity that moves and inspires people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You 're a prolific composer . Other times , writing is something that just comes to me &amp;mdash ; that , as I&amp;rsquo ; ve heard many other writers say , is written through me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What musical ambitions do you have ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I would like to spend some time writing larger suites for my small groups and writing more music for my new Electric band . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Tell me a bit about the musicians coming with you to Ottawa , and the material you 'll play . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I like playing with musicians from diverse backgrounds , experiences , and age groups . Martin Heslop is an in-demand Montreal bassist who also co-owns the R&amp;eacute ; sonance Cafe , and Wali Muhammad is a leading Montreal drummer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The music will be a collection of standards and my originals , a combination of modern straight-ahead and Latin tunes , with some odd-meter tunes and some ballads . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Dan Faulk Quartet&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Saturday , Oct. 26 , 7:30 p.m. &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Gigspace ( 953 Gladstone Ave. ) &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets : &lt;/strong&gt; $25 at gigspace.ca or at the door &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;13290;TOOLONG " **32;13317;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumWed , 23 Oct 2019 13:52:26 **45;13351;TOOLONG ... ArtsConcert review : Ogresse , C ? cile McLorin Salvant 's collaboration with Darcy James Argue , was flawlesshttp : **32;13398;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;13432;TOOLONG ... title= " C ? cile McLorin Salvant " alt= " C ? cile McLorin Salvant " data-portal-copyright= " John Abbott " **28;13468;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1481435 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver-based jazz broadcaster Nou Dadoun was in New York late last month for the most recent performance of Ogresse , vocalist C&amp;eacute ; cile McLorin Salvant&amp;rsquo ; s ambitious and spellbinding song cycle . He passes on this detailed review : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **36;13498;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Rose Hall , Jazz At Lincoln Center&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Reviewed Friday , Sept. 28&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;There 's a woman&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Lived in the woods&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;On the outskirts of town&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Her skin was chocolate brown&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Upon her head she wore a crown&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;of bones , human bones&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;She lived alone&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;With the birds and the trees&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;With her memories&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thus begins Ogresse , a fairy tale worthy of the Brothers Grimm that tells the story of a creature whose loneliness makes her ravenous . Her story is a song cycle filled with longing , love , betrayal , and drama . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ogresse is a unique collaboration between its composer and vocalist C&amp;eacute ; cile McLorin Salvant and bandleader/composer Darcy James Argue , who arranged it . In performance , Argue conducted the nine-piece L&amp;rsquo ; Orchestre Ogresse in combination with the Mivos String Quartet , an ensemble that has built its own reputation for collaborations with creative artists like experimental vocalist Jen Shyu. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McLorin Salvant and Argue share a stylistic flair that leans toward large statements in fashion , art , music and storytelling and Ogresse is operatic in scope . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McLorin Salvant has a voice that comes along only once or twice in a generation . It has passed through training in classical and formal technique but also takes on a remarkable expressiveness . A deserved darling of dozens of critics&amp;rsquo ; and popular polls , she won the Thelonious Monk International Jazz Vocals Competition in 2010 , when she was just 21. followed by two vocal jazz Grammy Awards before she turned 30. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Argue&amp;rsquo ; s compositions are expansive and most often realized through his own large ensemble the Secret Society . They are complex but with strong melodic lines that coalesce around the steampunk imagery of Infernal Machines , the overblown attempt to build the world&amp;rsquo ; s largest carousel in Brooklyn Babylon ( a multi-media production in collaboration with visual artist Danijel Zezelj ) or the modern political paranoia of Real Enemies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s a direct line from Gil Evans through Bob Brookmeyer and Maria Schneider in Argue&amp;rsquo ; s arrangements . The quality of his work has also been recognized in a series of Grammy and Juno Award nominations , in appearances of the Secret Society at major festivals like the Newport Jazz Festival and commissions from other adventurous ensembles like the Hard Rubber Orchestra . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We attended the Friday performance , the first of two on the last weekend in September at Rose Theater at Jazz at Lincoln Center In New York . The Theater is a beautiful wood-paneled space in an oval shape with about 1,200 seats that fan away from the stage in semi-circles and surround it with balconies . The wood and closeness of the performers enhanced the intimacy and closeness of the story &amp;mdash ; like watching a fairy tale play out in a field under the stars . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; L&amp;rsquo ; Orchestre Ogresse was assembled on stage when we entered . McLorin Salvant arrived in a luminous gown and commanded the stage with the ensemble in a semi-circle behind her and the story began . The song cycle was episodic in form and many of the episodes began with a country-twanged claw-hammer banjo playing a down-home introduction . Several of the later episodes had that same theme picked up by different parts of the Orchestra , here the string quartet and there the marimba. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The fairy tale was told by McLorin Salvant in alternating voices &amp;mdash ; an omniscient narrator , the Ogresse herself , her deceptive suitor and the birds who warned all of betrayal and disaster . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ogresse lives in the woods outside a town of wary and suspicious folk who can not believe how vast she is &amp;mdash ; her mouth is the size of a planet . And when the townspeople become too curious or try to catch her , she simply pops them inside that planet-sized mouth . She revels in her enormity but still she is lonely with only the trees and birds to keep her company . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the townsmen conspires against her and tries to subdue her with sweet words and love . She is resistant &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; I do not believe you , why should I believe you ? &amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; but he persists and eventually wears her down through her longing and loneliness . She dreams of dancing with him , hand in hand under clouds of violet , in a graveyard with bones underfoot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a heart-stopping moment , the birds reveal his treachery with a damning accusation : &amp;ldquo ; The Man is Lying ! &amp;rdquo ; In her despair and betrayal , the Ogresse poisons and consumes him &amp;ndash ; poisoning herself in a rage that consumes them both in an ultimate conflagration. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McLorin Salvant was the only vocalist but her power and expressiveness didn&amp;rsquo ; t not flag at all during the uninterrupted 90-minute performance . At the end , her hand holding the microphone gradually dropped to her side and her clear , un-amplified voice still filled the theatre completely . The perfect acoustics of Rose Theater supported the way in which she inhabited and acted out the different parts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a bonus , the libretto was handed out at the end of the performance in a small hand-printed booklet that was illustrated with Salvant&amp;rsquo ; s evocative sketches , revealing levels of nuance and wordplay that were easy to miss in the drama of the performance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The music drew on multiple influences &amp;mdash ; that recurring country-folk banjo theme , elements of Prokofiev and Mancini , and even a baroque interlude . The powerful dissonance in the scene of the final conflagration was riveting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was lots of solo space for these outstanding players . Highlights were Kirk Knuffke&amp;rsquo ; s cornet , Warren Wolf&amp;rsquo ; s vibes and marimba and Aaron Diehl&amp;rsquo ; s piano , chamber organ and melodica . In addition to the recurring themes , Nate Radley took an amazing banjo solo which was reminiscent of a koto , adding to the kabuki sense of drama . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In these days where so much adventurous large ensemble music suffers from a lack of rehearsal or unachieved ambition , it was a real pleasure to hear this creative endeavour totally engaging on so many levels in a flawless performance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The next opportunity to experience Ogresse is on Warren Wolf&amp;rsquo ; s home turf of SFJazz in San Francisco in March of 2020 . In the interim , Argue brings the Secret Society to New York City&amp;rsquo ; s Jazz Standard on Oct. 24. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McLorin Salvant has a West Coast tour that brings her and the Aaron Diehl trio to North Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Blueshore Centre for the Performing Arts on Oct. 16 and 17 . Then she spends November in Europe before returning to New York for a recording session and performance at Carnegie Hall with the new collective Artemis . If either ( or both ) come anywhere near you , don&amp;rsquo ; t pass up the opportunity to see them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Are you listening Mr. Pulitzer ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; C&amp;eacute ; cile McLorin Salvant , vocals , composer &lt;br&gt; with L&amp;rsquo ; Orchestre Ogresse &lt;br&gt; Darcy James Argue , bandleader , arranger , conductor &lt;br&gt; Alexa Tarantino , winds &lt;br&gt; Tom Christensen , winds &lt;br&gt; Kirk Knuffke , cornet &lt;br&gt; Josh Roseman , trombone , tuba &lt;br&gt; Nate Radley , guitar , banjo &lt;br&gt; Aaron Diehl , piano , melodica , organ &lt;br&gt; David Wong , bass &lt;br&gt; Samuel Torres , percussion &lt;br&gt; Warren Wolf , vibraphone , marimba &lt;br&gt; MIVOS String Quartet &lt;br&gt; Olivia De Prato , Maya Bennardo , violins &lt;br&gt; Victor Lowrie Tafoya , viola &lt;br&gt; Tyler J. Borden , cello &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumThu , 17 Oct 2019 19:36:38 **45;13536;TOOLONG ... University 's $200,000 Improv Workshop Project takes on life of its own , says Jean-Michel Pilchttp : **36;13583;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;13621;TOOLONG ... title= " Montreal-based pianist Jean-Michel Pilc " alt= " Montreal-based pianist Jean-Michel Pilc " data-portal-copyright= " Steve Sussman " **28;13657;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1284110 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " doctext " &gt;When jazz pianist Jean-Michel Pilc joined &lt;/span&gt; McGill University&amp;rsquo ; s Schulich School of Music in 2015 , he found out that being a professor also meant applying for peer-reviewed grants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I said , &amp;lsquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s not exactly the thing that I know best how to do . But I&amp;rsquo ; ll try , ' &amp;rdquo ; recalls Pilc , 58 , who was born in France and then spent two decades playing and teaching in New York City before moving to Montreal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pilc formulated a proposal , enlisted the help of a professional grant writer , and applied to the Fonds de R&amp;eacute ; cherche du Qu&amp;eacute ; bec &amp;ndash ; Soci&amp;eacute ; t&amp;eacute ; et culture . The fund&amp;rsquo ; s assessors liked what they saw and awarded Pilc&amp;rsquo ; s project $200,000. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was surprised as you are , &amp;rdquo ; Pilc says . &amp;ldquo ; I was elated and surprised and also a bit scared , because right now , I have to deliver the goods . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Outside of academia , Pilc is internationally renowned in jazz circles for his boldly unfettered and virtuosic music-making , usually in solo or trio contexts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;13687;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;13723;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; However , the point of his research project &amp;mdash ; dubbed the Improv Workshop Project , or IWP &amp;mdash ; is to study how a larger ensemble of seven or eight people can &amp;ldquo ; find ways to make great music that&amp;rsquo ; s not planned in advance at all , or very little . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The IWP is entering the third of its three years and will perform in Montreal Thursday night at Le Minist&amp;egrave ; re ( 4521 Boul . Saint-Laurent ) as part of L&amp;rsquo ; Off Festival de Jazz de Montr&amp;eacute ; al . The project also frequently plays at Resonance Caf&amp;eacute ; on Tuesday nights , and its upcoming gigs there are on Oct. 29 and Nov. 12. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The project draws from a diverse group of about 50 musicians , Pilc says . Along with him , key players are fellow McGill jazz professors Kevin Dean , who usually plays trumpet in a hard-bop style , and alto saxophonist R&amp;eacute ; mi Bolduc , who is equally at home playing swinging jazz in the style of Oscar Peterson or intricately plotted , even mathematical music . McGill music students and recent alumni , naturally , are involved in the project en masse . Occasionally , special guests join in , such as New York vocalist Elisabeth Kontomanou , who will sing with the project Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the past , saxophonist Sam Newsome and violinist Meg Okura , both U.S. musicians , have joined the IWP. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;13759;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;13795;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; One of the spurs for Pilc&amp;rsquo ; s project was his disinterest in jazz that strikes him as overly pre-conceived. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My frustration when I listen to most of modern jazz is that things tend to be very controlled , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; The compositions are very complex in general &amp;mdash ; lots of odd meters , exotic chord progressions and so forth &amp;mdash ; and people tend to write a lot before they even step foot on stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Even though the players might be fantastic and the music might be great , I always feels there is something that I personally am looking for in music and I don&amp;rsquo ; t find in that type of situation as a listener . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pilc says he&amp;rsquo ; s far from the first person to plumb free music , made without written material to lean on . But he says that he wanted to avoid &amp;ldquo ; what I call free jazz , which means people make all kinds of noises and there is not much melody and rhythm or if there is , it can be a bit chaotic , everybody plays all the time and in the same time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wanted to go and see how by improvising completely with such a group of people , we could create something that sounds really like a composition , like something that actually could have been written beforehand . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With willing collaborators , Pilc has met on more or less a weekly basis , recording sessions on video to scrutinize the process after the heat of the moment . Participants keep journals of their experiences , adding another dimension to the project . All aspects of the project are posted at its website , &lt;a href= " http : **27;13831;TOOLONG " &gt;im ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most of the project&amp;rsquo ; s participants , while conversant in jazz playing , are less familiar with entirely improvised playing . Pilc counts himself among them . &amp;ldquo ; To be quite honest with you , until recent years , I was myself scared to do it , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But it&amp;rsquo ; s interesting , those people are going to want to discover something about themselves that they didn&amp;rsquo ; t know before . They&amp;rsquo ; re going to participate to the collective &amp;lsquo ; writing , &amp;rsquo ; in the moment , which in my mind is what this project is about . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I call it paperless instant composition if you want to be more specific , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the fall of 2018 , a year after the project was launched , it landed the regular gig at Resonance Cafe . &amp;ldquo ; We got lucky , &amp;rdquo ; Pilc says . &amp;ldquo ; That changed completely the course of the project to me , because playing live every other week changed completely the spirit . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So far , the project has yielded several big discoveries , Pilc says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first is that the project &amp;ldquo ; has a personality , almost like it was a person , &amp;rdquo ; regardless of who is taking part , he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is this thing that transcends the musicians who are contributing , an interesting phenomenon of a certain mental state , that tends to instil itself , no matter who the musicians are . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Secondly , Pilc says the project has helped him rediscover the importance of the the most basic fundamentals of music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We had to use very simple techniques and ideas so that the music would really work , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; " T&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;he simpler the original idea , the better the music , in the way ... &lt;/span&gt; Even if the music ends up being very complex , the original idea at the core of that music was simple . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Simple melodies , simple rhythms , simple chords , simple ideas&amp;hellip ; simple anything . Simplicity leads to clarity , I think , &amp;rdquo ; Pilc says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He continues : &amp;ldquo ; My goal for the last year of this project will be to go toward even more simplicity . To make music that&amp;rsquo ; s even clearer , that&amp;rsquo ; s even more transparent , that&amp;rsquo ; s less encumbered by unnecessary clutter or overplaying of you know , just notes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think we&amp;rsquo ; re on the right path to that . The veteran Ottawa jazz musician has played on many CDs but at last is putting out his first CD solely under his own name later this month ( Jean Levac/ Ottawa Citizen ) " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;14101;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 727075 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; From the late 1960s to the late 1990s , Toronto-based trombonist and bandleader Rob McConnell and his Boss Brass big band loomed large over the Canadian jazz scene . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The **25;14131;TOOLONG ensemble was , in the words of its trumpeter Guido Basso , &amp;ldquo ; the only Canadian jazz band that could cross the border and play the living daylights out of U.S. musicians . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;14158;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;14194;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; After almost 30 albums , the band called it quits . McConnell recorded five more albums into the early 2000s . He died in 2010 , at the age of 75. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But his memory will live on , thanks to musicians such as Ottawa trombonist , pianist and bandleader Mark Ferguson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At his Saturday night performance at GigSpace , the intimate 46-seat performance space on Gladstone Avenue , Ferguson will be paying tribute to McConnell , who was something of a mentor to him . Below , Ferguson describes his relationship to McConnell and his music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Why are you paying tribute to Rob McConnell ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Rob was a major influence on me and I consider him to be one of the icons of jazz . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What will your tribute entail ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Usually when people pay tribute to him , it&amp;rsquo ; s in the format of a big band concert because arranging music for the Boss Brass is the thing for which Rob is most well-known . On Saturday , we&amp;rsquo ; ll be playing compositions written by Rob as well as a couple of his favourite standards that he played often in small group settings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What were your first contacts with McConnell 's music and with him personally ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : In the early 1970s when I was getting interested in jazz , the CRTC introduced Canadian content rules for radio and TV . Suddenly there were several TV variety shows produced in Toronto . I kept seeing the same musicians : Rob McConnell , Moe Koffman , Guido Basso , Jimmy Dale , Ed Bickert , Don Thompson and Terry Clarke . I was fascinated by the fact that Rob played the valve trombone and was blown away by his sound and his ability to swing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;14230;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;14266;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; When I was 19 , I attended a Phil Nimmons clinic in Fredericton , N.B. , so I could meet Rob and get some lessons with him . We developed almost a father-son type relationship . He had the reputation of being crusty and impatient with people but he was always kind to me . Meeting him inspired me to move to Toronto and study at Humber College . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How has McConnell influenced your trombone playing and your composing and arranging ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Living in Toronto in the 1980s , I attended countless Boss Brass concerts and heard Rob play in jazz clubs many times with small groups . I was hired a few times to sub in the Boss Brass trombone section , which was a total thrill for me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the early 1990s I received a Canada Council for the Arts grant to study arranging with Rob . During the lessons , I got a lot of insight into how he approached composition and arranging . He was hard on me and didn&amp;rsquo ; t pull any punches when he thought my work was substandard . It was exactly what I needed at the time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What did you do to pull together the material for Saturday 's concert ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I had a lot of fun transcribing Rob&amp;rsquo ; s compositions for this concert . As far as I know , they&amp;rsquo ; re not available in print and I prefer learning tunes from recordings rather than just reading them anyway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : On Oct. 20 , you 'll be playing at Merrickville 's Jazz Fest , but in a quartet with Ottawa saxophonist Mike Tremblay . What will that gig entail ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : We&amp;rsquo ; ll be performing original material from our recently released CD , Appleface . It&amp;rsquo ; s an unusual title that makes reference to Mike&amp;rsquo ; s wife&amp;rsquo ; s horse . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mike and I made a duo recording in 2008 that consisted of music associated with the great jazz pianist Bill Evans . For Appleface , we decided to record all originals composed by either me or Mike . We have a great friendship , and I think it affects our musical communication in a very positive way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Mark Ferguson Trio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Saturday , Oct. 12 , 7:30 p.m. &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; GigSpace ( 953 Gladstone Ave. ) &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets : &lt;/strong&gt; $25 at &lt;a href= " http : //gigspace.ca " &gt;gigspace.ca&lt;/ ... or at the door &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Mark Ferguson / Tremblay Quartet&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Sunday , Oct. 20 , 4 p.m. &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Merrickville United Arts Centre &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and festival passes : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **27;14302;TOOLONG " &gt;me ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;14331;TOOLONG " **32;14358;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **28;14392;TOOLONG " &gt;o ... &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumWed , 09 Oct 2019 13:54:07 **45;14422;TOOLONG ...
