ArtsConcert review : Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science at the TD Ottawa Jazz Festivalhttp : **32;19817;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19851;TOOLONG ... title= " Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science at the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " alt= " Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science at the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " data-portal-copyright= " Dan Nawrocki " **28;19887;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1420535 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science &lt;br&gt; TD Ottawa Jazz Festival &lt;br&gt; TD Main Stage &lt;br&gt; Reviewed Thursday &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Resistance music collided with the rain Thursday night when Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science played the TD Ottawa Jazz Festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The American drummer and her potent , uncompromising band played gritty , politically charged songs that combined rap , rock and jazz to combat racial injustice , intolerance and other ills . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The protest music , however , met with few ears . Thursday was the first rainy night at the jazz festival , and the sparse crowd had arrived to take in Carrington&amp;rsquo ; s band only thinned out further once the lightning flashed and the rain came down . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A potent force in jazz since her days as a teenaged prodigy in the early 1980s , Carrington , who has shared bandstands with Herbie Hancock , Wayne Shorter and Geri Allen . Most recently , she been a crusader on and off the bandstand for a more just society , with her Social Science project responding vocally and fiercely to the fraying of America in the time of Trump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19917;TOOLONG ... title= " Drummer Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science at the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " alt= " Drummer Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science at the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " data-portal-copyright= " Dan Nawrocki " **28;19953;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1420535 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; But in Ottawa Thursday night , the response to her music was subdued . Maybe a more woke audience on a less inclement evening would have sent the band the kind of energy that would have confirmed that its music was getting over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I know that some of this music is a little heavy , some of the messages . But I hope it&amp;rsquo ; s OK , &amp;rdquo ; Carrington said at one point , sounding just a wee bit Canadian . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This was a concert that began with a steely lament . &amp;ldquo ; This is for Donald , &amp;rdquo ; Debo Ray announced , before singing lyrics to a piece of elegiac but unbowed proportions that could only be aimed at her president . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; How much can we endure ? Time will tell , &amp;rdquo ; Ray sang . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; ll suffer through then rise again . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19983;TOOLONG ... title= " Vocalist Debo Ray of drummer Terri Lyne Carrington 's project Social Science at the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " alt= " Vocalist Debo Ray of drummer Terri Lyne Carrington 's project Social Science at the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " data-portal-copyright= " Dan Nawrocki " **28;20019;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1420534 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; This song and many that followed presented a new kind of blues for 2019 . Ray , always compelling , and Kassa Overall , the band&amp;rsquo ; s DJ and rapper , seemed to target one burning issue after another . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bells , a slow , hypnotic and ultimately tragic piece by Carrington&amp;rsquo ; s keyboardist Aaron Parks , was the underpinning for what seemed to be Ray&amp;rsquo ; s response to the killings of black men by police . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You took my love away from me , &amp;rdquo ; she sang . &amp;ldquo ; Tell me what give you the right to kill so senselessly ? &amp;rdquo ; If the song&amp;rsquo ; s words were open to interpretation , the closing sound of a siren helped to frame them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another piece allowed the band&amp;rsquo ; s voices to juxtapose two seemingly contradictory slogans &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; pray the hate away&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; pray the gay away . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the middle of its set , Carrington&amp;rsquo ; s band covered two love songs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First came a tune that Carrington referred to as &amp;ldquo ; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;something that you might actually recognize . " Perhaps her read of the crowds was that they were jazz fans first and social justice warriors second . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What followed was a rendition of the jazz standard What&amp;rsquo ; s New , ushered in gorgeously by Parks before it became the backdrop for Overall&amp;rsquo ; s spoken-word artistry . His commitment to his poetic rapping was clear , even if his voice could have been higher in the mix . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then came the group&amp;rsquo ; s version of the Joni Mitchell tune Love , on which Ray rose to the challenge . Carrington said that earlier in the day , she received clearance to put the Mitchell tune on her band&amp;rsquo ; s forthcoming record , which is to be released in November . In concert , the tune allowed instrumentalists Parks and Stevens to stretch out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Closing the concert of 70 or so minutes was a collaboration by Parks and Overall called Trapped in the American Dream , which offered a moody meditation on &amp;ldquo ; black and white&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; right and wrong . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kudos to the jazz festival for programming Carrington , a booking utterly in sync with the event&amp;rsquo ; s aspirations to be more gender-balanced . It was frustrating , though , that a small and rain-battered crowd was one factor that helped rob the night of the dynamism and urgency that it deserved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;20049;TOOLONG " **32;20076;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumFri , 28 Jun 2019 15:09:52 **45;20110;TOOLONG ... ArtsConcert review : Brad Mehlau Quintet at the TD Ottawa Jazz Festivalhttp : **32;20157;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20191;TOOLONG ... title= " Pianist Brad Mehldau , plays the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival , " alt= " Pianist Brad Mehldau , plays the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival , " data-portal-copyright= " Michael Wilson " **28;20227;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1418497 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brad Mehldau Quintet &lt;br&gt; TD Ottawa Jazz Festival &lt;br&gt; TD Main Stage &lt;br&gt; Reviewed Wednesday &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Marion Dewar Plaza on Wednesday night , pianist Brad Mehldau and his bandmates returned to their roots but didn&amp;rsquo ; t relive the past . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The revered 48-year-old American pianist , a leading jazz light of his generation for half of his life , was on the main stage with old and new friends , playing the kind of hard bop tunes that they had in all likelihood cut their teeth on as teenagers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But now , they approached the classic material not just to render it correctly as per the style of yesteryear&amp;rsquo ; s jazz and as other musicians might rigorously take as their mandate . Instead , they tackled the music with all the contemporary liberties and effusive personality of world-class musicians with nothing to prove anymore . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mehldau , tenor saxophonist Joel Frahm , trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire , bassist Joe Sanders and drummer Leon Parker also provided a welcome jazz incursion on the TD Main Stage , making &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; the kind of acoustic instrumental music that once prevailed during the festival 's long-running Concerts Under the Stars series , but which has since been displaced by more mass-appeal sounds . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mehldau and his new group , which was playing its eighth gig after forming earlier this month , drew a receptive , beyond-mid-sized crowd to the plaza . Sure , the audience was smaller than the plaza-filling multitude that took in Chicago and Norah Jones earlier during the festival . But Mehldau&amp;rsquo ; s quintet delivered musical delights that the others did not , including warm , glowing swinging and the overarching feeling that anything could happen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One thing is certain . Mehldau and his listeners were united by relief that the bad weather forecast for the evening ( severe thunderstorms with the possibility of a tornado ) never materialized . Instead , the night was perfect for enjoying jazz of impeccable lineage and abundant creativity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The quintet&amp;rsquo ; s lengthy set consisted of : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Blues in C ( Brad Mehldau ) &lt;br&gt; Besame Mucho ( Consuelo Vel&amp;aacute ; zquez ) &lt;br&gt; Chain Reaction ( Hank Mobley ) &lt;br&gt; Pannonica ( Thelonious Monk ) &lt;br&gt; Straight Ahead ( Kenny Dorham ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Encore : &lt;br&gt; Straight Street ( John Coltrane ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The opener set the tone for the night as the band delved into the most time-honoured tune form in jazz but found a world of possibilities in its 12 bars . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The music was roomy , patient and malleable , rooted in the jazz language but open to all kinds of spontaneous , organic feints and departures . It didn&amp;rsquo ; t take long for new harmonies , bass notes and grooves to shunt aside the usual ones . Mehldau , Akinmusire and Frahm uncorked solos that were grounded in the chosen material but wended far afield . The rhythm section&amp;rsquo ; s backdrop behind soloists morphed thanks to in-the-moment decisions , not the least of which were choices by Mehldau , Sanders or Parker not to play . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Throughout the night , highlights abounded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was the way in which Mehldau and Frahm , whose musical history dates back to their high school days in Connecticut , played the blues while not playing the blues on the pianist&amp;rsquo ; s Ornette Coleman-ish blues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was Akinmusire&amp;rsquo ; s hyper-motific solo on Besame Mucho , which Mehldau had recast as a bright , lilting waltz &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; a beautiful romantic song , &amp;rdquo ; he later announced &amp;mdash ; for which he rendered the melody . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also on Besame Mucho , there was Mehldau&amp;rsquo ; s extended , swaggering cruise on the tune&amp;rsquo ; s outro , which was a charged and juicy rejoinder to anyone who thought he had been holding back in this quintet format . ( He was the uncontested star when his trio played the jazz festival&amp;rsquo ; s main stage twice in the 2000s. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was Frahm&amp;rsquo ; s fondness for quotes , which on the Mobley-penned Minor Blues included permutations of Surrey with the Fringe on Top , Invitation and Witch Hunt &amp;mdash ; but who&amp;rsquo ; s counting ? Of course , apart from its puckish quoting , Frahm&amp;rsquo ; s playing bubbled over with ear-catching inventiveness and robust , positive feeling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was Parker&amp;rsquo ; s&amp;nbsp ; body percussion / human beat box tour de force on Straight Ahead , the rhythm changes-based tune that in the hands of Mehldau&amp;rsquo ; s band was not so straight ahead , yet straight ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On any given tune , there was Parker&amp;rsquo ; s stripped down but incredibly propulsive and centred playing . A few seconds of his buoyant ride cymbal playing had as much impact as a fusillade of notes from many other drummers . It wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be surprising if one big reason for Mehldau&amp;rsquo ; s band playing this month was the pianist&amp;rsquo ; s wish to reunite with the one-of-a-kind drummer with whom , if I&amp;rsquo ; m not mistaken , he&amp;rsquo ; d last made music with in the 1990s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Come to think of it , there was also Parker&amp;rsquo ; s transfixing introduction from behind his kit to Straight Ahead , which made it feel for a moment like all was right in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mehldau and his peers are often involved in more high-stakes music , playing more illustrious halls and making records for posterity that jazz tastemakers evaluate as state of the art . The pianist&amp;rsquo ; s latest projects have been staggeringly ambitious , adjoining his own improvising with the music of Bach or crafting unique , hard-hitting electronic protest music to bear witness in the time of Trump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;20257;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20299;TOOLONG ... preview : Eclectic Brad Mehldau takes inspiration from hard bop , Bible , Trump era&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wednesday night&amp;rsquo ; s concert was more low-key and admirably loose than all of that , about playing jazz because sometimes jazz is all you need . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Mehldau quintet has one more concert on its itinerary , at the Montreal International Jazz Festival tonight . The smart money is on it being super-heavy without trying to be heavy . But what will happen after ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This will really be a try-and-see venture , &amp;rdquo ; Mehldau told this newspaper before his band played its mid-June week at the Village Vanguard in New York . &amp;ldquo ; If it works out and everybody enjoys it , I imagine we&amp;lsquo ; d like to continue with more gigs. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We can only hope that Mehldau&amp;rsquo ; s quintet doesn&amp;rsquo ; t wink out of existence after tonight . But if that&amp;rsquo ; s the case , it will have left beautiful memories . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;20334;TOOLONG " **32;20361;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **28;20395;TOOLONG " &gt;o ... &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumThu , 27 Jun 2019 15:33:15 **45;20425;TOOLONG ... ArtsJazzfest preview : Eclectic Brad Mehldau takes inspiration from hard bop , Bible , Trump erahttp : **37;20472;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20511;TOOLONG ... title= " Pianist Brad Mehldau , who plays the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " alt= " Pianist Brad Mehldau , who plays the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20547;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1418499 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;20577;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pianist Brad Mehldau is a do-just-about-anything musician who can apply his brilliance equally to swinging , bop-based jazz , Bach-inspired improvising or trippy , hard-driving , electronic music with a distinctly socio-political thrust . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;20613;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20649;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;20685;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20721;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;20757;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20793;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Given his eclectic abilities , the news tidbit this spring that Mehldau , 48 , would debut a new , star-studded quintet in June at New York&amp;rsquo ; s legendary Village Vanguard jazz club , and soon after play selected Canadian jazz festivals with the group , prompted curiosity and speculation , above all about what kind of music he would play . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I am as curious as you are , &amp;rdquo ; said Petr Cancura , programming manager of TD Ottawa Jazz Festival , where Mehldau&amp;rsquo ; s quintet will play Wednesday night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It got confirmed pretty late that it ( the booking ) was in fact going to be a quintet , &amp;rdquo ; Cancura said . &amp;ldquo ; For the longest time it was going to be his usual trio . &amp;rdquo ; Mehldau played the Ottawa festival with his trio in 2002 , 2006 and 2008 , and then returned most recently to Ottawa with saxophonist Joshua Redman in 2011. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below , Mehldau sheds light on what his new band will play in Marion Dewar Plaza , and talks about his just-released album , Finding Gabriel &amp;mdash ; an entirely different project that converts Bible-inspired notions into unique , modern protest music that embraces contemporary grooves , synth-y textures and choral singing alike . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Why have you formed this new band ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I&amp;lsquo ; ve admired all these players for a number of years . ( Saxophonist ) Joel ( Frahm ) is the one I&amp;lsquo ; ve known longest , since we were 15 years old and played together in high school . ( Drummer ) Leon ( Parker ) and I played together a lot in a trio in 1990 and &amp;rsquo ; 91 , during my first years in New York City . ( Trumpeter ) Ambrose ( Akinmusire ) and ( bassist ) Joe ( Sanders ) I&amp;rsquo ; ve followed for a few years , Joe particularly in his work with pianist Gerald Clayton . Ambrose I&amp;rsquo ; ve gotten to record with twice , with ( guitarist ) Wolfgang Muthspiel , and the experience was fantastic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;20829;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20864;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What material will this group play ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : My idea with this band is to begin more simply , and not try to reinvent the wheel in terms of composition . In that way we can have a common starting point as a band . We&amp;lsquo ; ll play some of my tunes and some standards and some material from the hard-bop era &amp;mdash ; a few early Coltrane tunes , Clifford Brown , Oliver Nelson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How will you ready the band before its first gig ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I&amp;lsquo ; ve made some arrangements and we will have one long rehearsal , and then bam &amp;mdash ; showtime. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : After your Canadian festival concerts , what hopes do you have for this group ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : This will really be a try-and-see venture . If it works out and everybody enjoys it , I imagine we&amp;lsquo ; d like to continue with more gigs. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Finding Gabriel draws upon your close reading of the Bible in recent years . Prior to that , how significant was the Bible in your life ? How religious are you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I believe in God but do not identify with any of the monotheistic religions specifically . I&amp;lsquo ; ve also found a lot of solace and guidance from Buddhist and Vedanta teachings . The Bible is more recent for me in terms of close reading and reflection . I had never read the prophetic books in the Old Testament until two years ago and was drawn into them , along with the Gospels and the Pauline letters of the New Testament . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What is it about recent times that prompted you to delve into the Bible ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : It is a moral guide for modern society whether one is a believer , atheist , conservative , or liberal . It is striking to see the parallels , the same questions being asked , the same answers being given , the same mistakes being made . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Were you concerned about releasing music that in some cases is so overtly political , and even anti-Trump ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : The scripture from Hosea that frames the anti-Trump song , The Prophet is A Fool , is meant to invoke the phenomenon of fake news : Hosea means that even if a prophet would be among us , we would call him a fool . In just over three years , our trust has begun to evaporate in institutions that are fundamental to democracy and free speech . Trump has said that the press is an &amp;ldquo ; enemy of the people , &amp;ldquo ; in the language of fascism . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;20900;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20936;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; I was concerned about a Trump supporter taking issue with that track . The important thing is , I&amp;lsquo ; m not coming down on Trump supporters . The music bears witness . I&amp;lsquo ; m bearing witness to xenophobia , racism and violence and how they have manifested in my society , a society I hold dear . I&amp;lsquo ; m inspired by the prophets , who were not afraid to judge Israel . I invite the listener to bear witness as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Do you have an ideal listener in mind for this music ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : My ideal listener , I suppose , would be one who acknowledges the danger of Trump&amp;rsquo ; s demagoguery. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Is it fair to consider the album as protest music , in the lineage of jazz albums such as Max Roach 's We Insist ! , Charles Mingus 's Fables of Faubus and Charlie Haden 's Not In Our Name , to name a few ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I&amp;lsquo ; d be proud to be included with Mingus anywhere , and the others ! The only thing I would qualify that with is that Finding Gabriel is also about a personal search , very much on a subjective level , that culminates on the final title track . So it&amp;lsquo ; s trying to bridge the personal with the political , and one person finding his way in all of that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of my favourite rock &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;lsquo ; roll moments is Gim me Shelter from The Rolling Stones . It&amp;lsquo ; s a protest song &amp;mdash ; maybe the only one they ever wrote . But it goes back to the first-person subject , who says &amp;ldquo ; Give me shelter&amp;rdquo ; from all of the turmoil . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Brad Mehldau Quintet&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; TD Ottawa Jazz Festival &lt;br&gt; When : Wednesday , June 26 , 8:30 p.m. &lt;br&gt; Where : TD Main Stage , Marion Dewar Plaza &lt;br&gt; Tickets : &lt;a href= " http : //ottawajazzfestival.com " &gt;ottaw ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;20972;TOOLONG " **32;20999;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;MORE ON JAZZFEST : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21033;TOOLONG ... preview : Ottawa saxophonist Alison Young balances jazz exploits with rocking out in Corey Hart 's band&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21068;TOOLONG ... preview : Christine Jensen leads the festival 's signature gender-balanced big band Tuesday&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21103;TOOLONG ... review : Chicago comes to Ottawa with new singer , and he 's Canadian&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumTue , 25 Jun 2019 20:13:54 **45;21138;TOOLONG ... ArtsJazzfest preview : Ottawa saxophonist Alison Young balances jazz exploits with rocking out in Corey Hart 's bandhttp : **36;21185;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;21223;TOOLONG ... title= " Ottawa-raised , Toronto-based saxophonist Alison Young , a Juno Award nominee and member of Corey Hart 's band , plays the TD Ottawa Jazz Festival on Thursday June 27 , 2019. " alt= " Ottawa-raised , Toronto-based saxophonist Alison Young , a Juno Award nominee and member of Corey Hart 's band , plays the TD Ottawa Jazz Festival on Thursday June 27 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Provided by Alison Young " **28;21259;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1418480 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;21289;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s been a banner year so far for saxophonist Alison Young , who scored a Juno nomination for her debut album , So Here We Are , and began rocking out on tour with Corey Hart . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The achievements are the latest milestones in a musical journey that includes growing up in the Glebe , playing in the Nepean All-City Jazz Band , and relocating to Toronto , where Young , 37 , studied music and has been gigging in the musical trenches since her early 20s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In advance of her TD Ottawa Jazz Festival concert Thursday , Young discusses the steps along her journey . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What were your first big musical experiences ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I started on piano around age six . I particularly loved Beethoven , and would wildly overdramatize his pieces , sacrificing technical perfection for passion . ( This habit may have stayed with me. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I was 12 , I heard big band music for the first time , courtesy of Hopewell&amp;rsquo ; s stage band , led by Allison Woyiwada . I instantly fell in love and begged my parents to rent me a saxophone . I discovered my parents&amp;rsquo ; Count Basie and Duke Ellington records and played along with them obsessively . At the time I never imagined I&amp;rsquo ; d become a musician , but I was fascinated by the sound of the sax section and the soloists , and needed to know how to make that sound and channel that feeling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By the time I finished high school , I was gigging a little bit around Ottawa and playing in the Nepean All-City Jazz Band , and loving every minute of it . I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t think of anything else I wanted to do . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Where did you study music and what did you get out of it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : &amp;nbsp ; I was ecstatic when I was accepted into the University of Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s jazz program , and then had a big wakeup call . Up until then I was mostly self-taught on the saxophone , and had a lot of catching up to do with regard to technique and theory . The faculty was stacked with great musicians , and Mike Murley and Kirk MacDonald were fantastic private teachers . The only thing I regret about university is that I was too terrified to get out and play more with my fellow students . I spent a lot of time in the practice rooms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How do you split your musical time and energies these days ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I do it all ! Jazz , blues , pop , R&amp;amp ; B , session work , commercials , you name it . I&amp;rsquo ; m fortunate in that I love many genres of music , and enjoy the challenge of fitting in to whatever I&amp;rsquo ; m called to play . To make a living as a gigging musician you need to stay busy , and it helps to be versatile . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The majority of my work is still as a sideman . I play regularly with a diverse bunch of projects&amp;nbsp ; ( Big Rude Jake , Heillig Manoeuvre , Alysha Brilla , Rita Chiarelli , Red Hot Ramble , Joe Sealy , Suzie McNeil , and Chelsea McBride&amp;rsquo ; s Socialist Night School among others ) and I love it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;21325;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;21361;TOOLONG &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;21397;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;21433;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m enjoying developing my voice as a leader , however , and devoting more time to composing and booking gigs of my own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What prompted you to put out your first album as a leader ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I had been gigging here and there as a leader , had found a great team of musicians ( shoutout to Jeff McLeod , Eric St-Laurent , Ross MacIntyre , Sly Juhas and Chris Wallace ! ) , and had written some compositions I liked , but never felt ready to put out an album . Now I know that feeling probably never goes away . The push came when I was awarded a free day of recording at Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s Canterbury Studios and had to get the band in the studio before the end of the year . I&amp;rsquo ; m so grateful for that opportunity and deadline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Your album 's an eclectic one . Why ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Going into the studio , I wasn&amp;rsquo ; t sure whether I wanted to lean more on my jazz influences or make a funkier , bluesier sounding record . We ended up doing both , and the band swings so hard . I&amp;rsquo ; m proud of how it turned out . My priority is always to tell a story , to find the joy and soul of the song , and communicate that to the listener . I hope we achieved that with this album . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What did that mean for you to have your album nominated for a Juno ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I half-jokingly said &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a confidence boost ! &amp;rdquo ; to an interviewer at the Juno Nominee announcement party , but it really has been that . It&amp;rsquo ; s an incredible honour to get recognized on a national level , especially since it&amp;rsquo ; s my first album . It means a lot to me ! I&amp;rsquo ; m hoping it will lead to more festival bookings for my band ( we&amp;rsquo ; re doing several this summer , which is exciting ) and ideally a Canadian tour in the near future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;21469;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;21505;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How did you come to tour with Corey Hart ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I got a phone call out of the blue last year from producer Bob Ezrin , asking if I wanted to record on Corey Hart&amp;rsquo ; s new EP . Uh , yes ! I was very young when he first rose to fame , but I remember loving Sunglasses at Night as a kid in the &amp;rsquo ; 80s , and having a cassette of The Singles . I went in to record a sax solo on the EP&amp;rsquo ; s title track , Dreaming Time Again , and to my surprise Corey was at the session , and asked me if I&amp;rsquo ; d be interested in coming on tour . Again , yes ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How would you compare playing with Hart to your jazz exploits ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;A : It 's a very different experience . It 's an amazing rush , playing to a stadium full of fans who know and love the songs . I 'm so used to the comparative looseness of a jazz setting , where changing directions on a whim is par for the course , and if you lose the thread , you create a new one . This is a different challenge ! You need to play with all the rock ' n ' roll energy and intent , but also nail the iconic solos . I 'm loving this tour . Corey and the band and the crew are fantastic to work with . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : The Ottawa Jazz Festival is striving this year to present a lineup with gender parity . What do you think of this goal ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I think it&amp;rsquo ; s a fabulous idea to consciously present a more gender-balanced lineup in the festival . There are so many deserving artists , both established and up-and-coming , and presenting more women artists can only help inspire the next generation of young female musicians to create music and feel like they belong . I remember seeing Christine Jensen play at the Ottawa festival as a teenager and being inspired by her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We are still underrepresented in jazz , but lately I see more young women players coming on the scene and killing it , and I like where this is headed . Hopefully in the future it won&amp;rsquo ; t have to be a conscious decision to have a more equal balance of males and females on the festival stage , but this is a great step . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Alison Young&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; TD Ottawa Jazz Festival &lt;br&gt; When : Thursday , June 27 , 6:30 p.m. &lt;br&gt; Where : TD Main Stage , Marion Dewar Plaza &lt;br&gt; Tickets : &lt;a href= " http : //ottawajazfestival.com " &gt;ottawa ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;21541;TOOLONG " **32;21568;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;MORE JAZZFEST : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21602;TOOLONG ... preview : Christine Jensen leads the festival 's signature gender-balanced big band Tuesday&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21637;TOOLONG ... review : Chicago comes to Ottawa with new singer , and he 's Canadian&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21672;TOOLONG ... review : New Orleans singer Erica Falls elevates Galactic fusion&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21707;TOOLONG ... review : Judith Hill and her funky family open it on a positive note&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumTue , 25 Jun 2019 17:09:05 **45;21742;TOOLONG ... ArtsJazzfest preview : Christine Jensen leads the festival 's signature , gender-balanced big band Tuesdayhttp : **33;21789;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;21824;TOOLONG ... title= " Montreal saxophonist/composer and bandleader Christine Jensen is in her creative prime . " alt= " Montreal saxophonist/composer and bandleader Christine Jensen is in her creative prime . " data-portal-copyright= " Randy Cole " **28;21860;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1149091 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;21890;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; When the distinctively named = Jazz Orchestra makes its debut Tuesday at the TD Ottawa Jazz Festival , it could not have a better woman at the helm than Christine Jensen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Montreal-based saxophonist and bandleader , 49 , has led her own jazz orchestra for more than a decade , winning a Juno Award for each of its two recordings . She and her sister , the world-class New York-based trumpeter Ingrid Jensen , have been role models for women in jazz in Canada and beyond since they made their first recordings in the 1990s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the NAC Studio on Tuesday night , the = Jazz Orchestra , a gender-balanced big band uniting musicians from Montreal , Ottawa and Toronto , will celebrate a subset of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s jazz sisterhood . In the band with Jensen are pianist Marianne Trudel , a fellow Montrealer , plus the Toronto-based horn players Allison Au , Tara Davidson and Rebecca Hennessy , and the New York City-based Canadian expat Anna Webber . The project is fully in sync with the jazz festival&amp;rsquo ; s goal of achieving gender parity in its bookings this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below , Jensen discusses the special project , which she hopes will be more than a one-off . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How did this new band come to be ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : It was a bit of a brainstorm that I was having with Petr Cancura at the Ottawa Jazz Festival , about presenting more of a balance in big bands , while looking at the future of where the music is going . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the same time , Petr and Catherine ( O&amp;rsquo ; Grady , the jazz festival&amp;rsquo ; s executive producer ) are really working on a balanced festival program this year with gender balance . I was at the Monterey Jazz Festival last year , and it was the most amazing balance going on there , with the greatest vibe among musicians and audience . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We started planning this winter , after I got really inspired after putting a really strong orchestra at the Oscar Peterson Jazz Festival . Its artistic director , the amazing Renee Rosnes , requested that I perform my music with a Toronto-based horn section . I was able to get four women in the horn section , plus Ingrid as soloist . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This time , I am able to get six very strong female voices out of the 13 horns , plus the amazing wizard of spontaneity Marianne Trudel , who is adding her music with some excerpts from the suite that she wrote a few years back for the orchestra national jazz de Montreal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Somehow the overall repertoire of this concert is , to me , &amp;ldquo ; the voice of the now , &amp;rdquo ; with compositions from Marianne , myself , Rebecca , Tara and Anna . Oh &amp;mdash ; we are adding Carla Bley&amp;rsquo ; s music , because her music is not performed enough outside of her own band . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Tell me about the connections you have or are about to have with some of the orchestra 's other women . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I love Marianne&amp;rsquo ; s energy . We float through different combinations of ensembles in Montreal and always have a lot of fun performing together . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anna was once in a McGill ensemble that I directed . I also love her energy and her quest , new music meeting improvisation at an extremely high level . Allison and Tara are gems , with equally strong composition and improv skills and great sound . They worked with me on my concert at the Oscar Peterson Jazz Festival with Renee , along with Rebecca , who is also going down a really creative path . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Do you hope you can get other bookings for this project down the road ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : It would be amazing to keep working on this concept of presenting living composers , with an even more even voice in composition and performance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Overall , what progress is being made in jazz in terms of combating discrimination against women and advancing gender issues ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : There&amp;rsquo ; s lots of pluses going on right now . These are changing times . Women still have a ways to go in breaking the glass ceiling on the main stage , and in the more elite jazz institutions . But there is a lot of work getting done with everyone becoming more conscious and finding solutions . There are more opportunities for young women to explore in a safe space with educational opportunities and jam spaces . Everyone , especially the younger generation of musicians , is so more aware . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;= Jazz Orchestra&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; TD Ottawa Jazz Festival &lt;br&gt; **33;21926;TOOLONG : Tuesday , June 25 , 7 p.m. &lt;br&gt; **34;21961;TOOLONG : NAC Studio &lt;br&gt; **36;21997;TOOLONG : ottawajazzfestival.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;22035;TOOLONG " **32;22062;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; twitter.com/peterhum &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22096;TOOLONG ... review : Chicago comes to Ottawa with new singer , and he 's Canadian&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22131;TOOLONG ... review : New Orleans singer Erica Falls elevates Galactic fusion&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22166;TOOLONG ...
